title: CYSTINOSIS, LATE-ONSET JUVENILE OR ADOLESCENT NEPHROPATHIC TYPE

relationships.phenotype: CYSTINOSIS, LATE-ONSET JUVENILE OR ADOLESCENT NEPHROPATHIC TYPE

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that late-onset juvenile or adolescent nephropathic cystinosis is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the CTNS gene (606272) on chromosome 17p13.2.

checks.claim: Late-onset juvenile or adolescent nephropathic cystinosis is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the CTNS gene.
checks.evidence_quote: The disease occurs due either to the combination of one mild mutation and one which is known to cause nephropathic cystinosis or to homozygosity for a predicted mild mutation.
checks.explanation: The abstract supports homozygous or compound heterozygous CTNS mutations for 'intermediate' cystinosis. It does not use the terms late-onset, juvenile or adolescent.

checks.claim: The CTNS gene is located on chromosome 17p13.2.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutations of CTNS causing intermediate cystinosis.
checks.explanation: The abstract names CTNS but does not give the chromosomal location. The location is standard nomenclature.

paragraphs.text: Thoene et al. (1999) described an intermediate form of cystinosis. It results either from one mild CTNS mutation combined with one mutation known to cause nephropathic cystinosis, or from homozygosity for a predicted mild mutation. Attard et al. (1999) stated that cystinosis is caused by a defect in the transport of cystine across the lysosomal membrane. They noted that structure predictions suggested the gene product, cystinosin, is a novel integral lysosomal membrane protein. According to Attard et al. (1999), late-onset cystinosis is a rarer form of the disorder, with symptoms beginning between 12 and 15 years of age.

paragraphs.text: Thoene et al. (1999) found that the intermediate form of cystinosis occurs either in compound heterozygotes for a mild CTNS mutation and a mutation known to cause nephropathic cystinosis, or in homozygotes for a predicted mild mutation. These biallelic genotypes imply autosomal recessive inheritance. Because affected individuals carry mutations known to cause nephropathic cystinosis, the intermediate form is allelic to nephropathic cystinosis.

checks.evidence_quote: The disease occurs due either to the combination of one mild mutation and one which is known to cause nephropathic cystinosis
checks.explanation: A combination of two different mutations is compound heterozygosity.

checks.evidence_quote: The disease occurs due either to the combination of one mild mutation and one which is known to cause nephropathic cystinosis or to homozygosity for a predicted mild mutation.
checks.explanation: The biallelic genotypes are stated. The abstract does not explicitly state autosomal recessive inheritance; this is an inference.

checks.evidence_quote: the combination of one mild mutation and one which is known to cause nephropathic cystinosis
checks.explanation: This supports allelism with nephropathic cystinosis. However, only the compound heterozygotes carry a nephropathic mutation; the homozygous mild-mutation patients do not.

paragraphs.text: Attard et al. (1999) identified CTNS mutations in patients with late-onset cystinosis. In their patients with infantile nephropathic cystinosis, the mutations on both alleles were predicted to cause loss of cystinosin function. These mutations included a common deletion of approximately 65 kb.

checks.claim: Attard et al. (1999) identified CTNS mutations in patients with late-onset cystinosis.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutations found in two late-onset patients affect functionally unimportant regions of cystinosin
checks.explanation: The abstract reports CTNS mutations found in two late-onset patients.

checks.claim: In the infantile nephropathic cystinosis patients of Attard et al. (1999), the CTNS mutations on both alleles were predicted to cause loss of cystinosin function.
checks.evidence_quote: 12 have two severely truncating mutations, which is consistent with a loss of functional protein, and 13 have missense or in-frame deletions, which would result in disruption of transmembrane domains and loss of protein function
checks.explanation: Loss of function is predicted for all 25 infantile patients. The abstract does not say that both alleles carry loss-of-function mutations in the 13 patients with missense mutations or in-frame deletions.

checks.claim: The CTNS mutations in the infantile nephropathic cystinosis patients of Attard et al. (1999) included a common deletion of approximately 65 kb.
checks.evidence_quote: identified pathogenic mutations in patients with infantile nephropathic cystinosis, including a common, approximately 65 kb deletion which encompasses exons 1-10
checks.explanation: The abstract presents the approximately 65 kb deletion as a finding from the authors' earlier work. It does not say the deletion was found in this study's patients.

paragraphs.text: Attard et al. (1999) found that the severity of the cystinosis phenotype varied with the mutations in the CTNS gene. Of 25 patients with infantile nephropathic cystinosis, 12 had two severely truncating mutations. The other 13 had missense mutations or in-frame deletions, which were predicted to disrupt transmembrane domains and cause loss of protein function. In two late-onset patients, the mutations affected functionally unimportant regions of cystinosin, which accounted for their milder phenotype.
